claims.head: The Golden Knights should tilt the ice
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Golden Knights’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward.

Nicolas Hague has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Daemon Hunt has taken his spot beside Jayden Struble. That pair has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 73:39 together, up from 29% with Hague.
Shane Wright joined from SEA on Nov 2 and has played beside Filip Forsberg and Nils Höglander.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.
Noah Hanifin is out week to week and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan.

stakes: The Predators go in second in the Central with 25 points, the Golden Knights second in the Pacific with 28 points.

VGK.head: The matchup suits the Golden Knights
VGK.body: Even though Vegas will be without Hanifin, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Predators’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Can anyone stop the Predators?
paras: The Predators are on a tear, six straight wins. Vegas has won four straight. The Golden Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Nashville on Oct 13. Going in, the Preds are second in the Central (ninth in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (fourth).
The Predators’ record (.658) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.533), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Golden Knights’ record (.700) is about what their chances are worth.
In their six-game winning streak, the Predators have outscored teams 21-10, including 15-9 at 5-on-5.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). They also give up a lot of shots (30th), so the Golden Knights have the edge over them on shot suppression. The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd) and create chances on the penalty kill (2nd). The Golden Knights’ power play against the Predators’ penalty killers is strength against strength.

Filip Forsberg (7 G / 15 A / 22 P in 19 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, and Steven Stamkos (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 19 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for eighth in the NHL. Jack Eichel (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 20 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, and Mark Stone (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 20 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

Juuse Saros (6-3-4 / .919 SV% in 13 GS) has been outstanding for Nashville and will likely start. Vegas has two options in net: Carter Hart (6-3-2 / .896 SV% in 11 GS) and Adin Hill (7-2-0 / .903 SV% in 9 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Hart got the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Golden Knights usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.
